builds.howItPlays: You play cheap units like Legion Marauder and Kayle, Justified early, then spend your spare runes to Empower them, paying a cost printed on the unit to make it stronger, and Kayle can take it three times, gaining 2 Might each time. Guttural Roar gives an Empowered unit +4 Might for the turn, and each time one of your units reaches 5 Might, Fiora gives you an extra rune to spend next turn.
builds.whyYou: You like attacking early, and you want your spare runes to go somewhere useful every turn instead of sitting there. You enjoy the small sums this deck asks for: which unit to Empower first, whether Guttural Roar or Punch First gets it to 5 Might, and whether the rune Fiora hands you pays for another Empower next turn. Your units start small and you don't mind, because a few turns in they are bigger than anything your opponent can block with. If growing a cheap board into a strong one while you score points sounds fun, this Fiora suits you.

builds.howItPlays: You spend your early turns on spells that give you extra runes, such as Mobilize and Sacrifice, which kills one of your own units with 5 or more Might to draw 2 cards and gain a rune, while Rampage and Riposte deal with what your opponent plays early. Once you can pay 9 for Dazzling Aurora, it plays the first unit from the top of your deck for free at the end of each of your turns, often Rift Herald or Elder Dragon, a 12-cost unit that kills an enemy unit at every location when it arrives.
builds.whyYou: You'd rather steer every early turn toward one big goal than fight for battlefields from the first turn. Killing one of your own units with Sacrifice doesn't bother you if it gets Dazzling Aurora down a turn sooner, and once it lands you enjoy seeing what the top of your deck hands you for free each turn. Some games Aurora never shows up, or your opponent destroys it, and you can live with that because the games where it survives are very hard to come back from. If a slow start that turns into a free big unit every turn sounds good, this Fiora suits you.
